thread:
Maria: :rotating_light: alert from ops-bot — Persephone VPC tenant 0x9a experiencing sustained 504s and correlation to model inference latency spikes. Errors started ~5m ago. Logs show KV cache misses and memory thrashing on pool-persephone-dedicated-2.
ops-bot: Incident created - ID INC-3087654321. Paging on-call (Alex). Severity: P1. Affected: dedicated pool (persephone), model: text-epoch-8-quant.
Alex (on-call): I'm on it, grabbing logs. Maria — what's the customer impact? Are requests failing end-to-end or just slow?
Maria: Persephone says ledger job retries are piling up, some user-facing failures in reconciliation (they reported duplicated transactions). So pretty bad for them. Errors: 504s + "context length exceeded" retries in some forks.
Chetan: from traces I'm seeing tail latency surges when sequence_length > 2048. The model variant text-epoch-8-quant has an aggressive kv-eviction setting; when eviction thrashes GPU memory we hit OOM and backend returns 504.
Rachel: Do we have a safe-variant available for this tenant that is latency-stable but maybe higher cost?
Samir: We can route to text-epoch-7-stable (fp16) — a bit older, slightly larger tokens cost, but stable kv behavior. We're currently out of capacity in the same pool for that variant, but we can spin up a small emergency slot in the per-tenant fallback pool.
Maria: Customer ops (Persephone Support) wants minimal data exposure, so we need the route to remain within their VPC/dedicated context if possible.
Persephone Support: Confirmed — please keep data inside our dedicated pool. We can accept a temporary larger instance in the same tenant if required.
Alex (on-call): OK plan proposal: (1) apply tenant-level override to pin model to text-epoch-7-stable for Persephone, (2) provision 2x emergency slots in per-tenant fallback cluster (p-dedicated-fallback), (3) set autoscale min to 2 for the tenant while we stabilize, (4) throttle batch size from 16->4 for the tenant.
Chetan: I can push the override. Quick config snippet:
```
{
  "tenant_id": "persephone-0x9a",
  "override": {
    "model": "text-epoch-7-stable",
    "routing_scope": "dedicated-pool",
    "batch_size": 4,
    "cache_policy": "pin-kv",
    "graceful_drain": true
  },
  "note": "Emergency mitigation - pin to stable variant while investigating kv thrash"
}
```
Rachel: After we pin, we should enable canary routing 10% for 5 minutes to ensure the stable variant responds correctly for ledger flows. If good, promote to 100%.
Samir: Provisioning fallback slots now — ETA ~3m. I'm using the internal playbook cmd: `infractl allocate slot --tenant persephone-0x9a --pool p-dedicated-fallback --count 2 --label emergency`
ops-bot: infractl job queued (job-7391). Estimated 210s.
Maria: Also notify Red team (SLA folks) and Support: Persephone ops please expect a short role-over window. We'll keep logs and audit entries for KMS key usage.
Persephone Support: Good. We'll stand by for the change window. Keep us updated on the canary results.
Alex (on-call): Chetan, once the override is applied, please watch the token-level latency for ledger-sync route and the 5xx rate. Use the console trace filter `route:persephone-ledger` and alert me if p50 > 400ms or error_rate > 0.5%.
Chetan: Applying tenant override now. Pushing config to control plane...
Chetan: Done — override accepted, id ov-3087-ps. Routing table updated to prefer text-epoch-7-stable for tenant persephone-0x9a.
ops-bot: rollout recorded (ov-3087-ps), canary set to 10% for 5m.
Maria: Samir — how are the fallback slots?
Samir: Slots ready, containers healthy. I added extra liveness probes and limited prefetch to avoid cold-start pressure.
Alex (on-call): Starting canary. We'll monitor errors and token latency. Rachel — can you run a quick synthetic ledger-run test? Use the internal harness: `harness run --target persephone-ledger --size 2k`
Rachel: Running now. First run shows p95 latency improved from 1.8s -> 480ms for canary traffic. Error rate dropped from 2.7% -> 0.2% on canary.
Persephone Support: Observing decreased failures on our side as well. Retry storm subsiding.
Maria: Great — canary looks good. Let's promote to 100% in 2m if metrics hold. Also enable temporary alert suppression for non-critical noise.
Alex (on-call): Promoting to 100% now.
ops-bot: Promotion recorded. Route updated. Audit logs: link https://console.redwood/ov-3087-ps/audit (redacted)
Chetan: Monitoring post-promotion. So far p50=220ms, p95=510ms, 5xx <= 0.3%. KV hit-rate improved after pinning. Looks like the older stable variant has more predictable cache behavior.
Samir: Autoscale min set to 2 for tenant. Batch limit enforced at 4.
Maria: Customer-facing update draft: "We detected elevated latency and errors affecting ledger reconciliation. We've temporarily pinned your tenant to a stable model variant and provisioned extra capacity inside your dedicated pool to restore normal operations. Our engineering team is continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary." Approve?
Persephone Support: Approved. Please include timeframe and the mitigation steps. We'll share internally.
Rachel: Adding follow-up tasks: (A) reproduce kv-eviction locally with synthetic traces, (B) bench text-epoch-8-quant with tuned kv-policy, (C) run regression evals comparing outputs between epoch-8 and epoch-7 to check for semantic deltas on ledger invariants.
Alex (on-call): Assigning tasks: Chetan(A), Samir(B), Rachel(C). I'll keep this incident open and own the handoff to engineering tomorrow morning at 0900 PT.
Maria: Also note: we should consider a short-term runtime flag to auto-fallback to stable variant on repeated kv-eviction detection for tenants with high-consistency workloads. Logged as RFC-1147.
Chetan: I'll attach traces and a minimal repro to the ticket.
Persephone Support: Thanks all — system behavior looks stable for now. We'll reach out if anything else pops.
ops-bot: Incident INC-3087654321 status -> mitigated (monitoring). Incident will be closed once postmortem is scheduled.
Alex (on-call): Closing notes: Mitigation successful. Customer impact reduced to sporadic retries, ledger sync backlog cleared. On-call handoff to day team tomorrow 09:00 PT (Rachel).
Maria: Thanks everyone. We'll keep the RFC and the post-incident writeup in the incident ticket.
Persephone Support: Appreciated.
Rachel: I'll own the postmortem and include the canary graphs, kv metrics, and the regression diff.
Samir: I'll also add the infra allocation cost delta for the emergency slots.
Alex (on-call): Adding final: If anyone sees a recurrence, page me immediately. :thumbsup:
